title: Long-time Dynamics of Many-body Open Quantum Systems using Quantum Generating Functions
authors: Katha Ganguly, Dario Poletti, Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract: The interplay between coherent unitary evolution and environment-induced dissipation can give rise to a wide range of non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems, ranging from interesting transport phenomena to dynamical phase transitions. However, accessing such long-time dynamics remains challenging for the existing methods developed for the simulation of many-body open quantum systems. We address this problem by developing a quantum generating function (QGF) formalism for open many-body systems for both ensemble-averaged dynamics governed by a Markovian quantum master equation and trajectory-resolved dynamics described by the quantum trajectory formalism, including quantum jumps, and quantum state diffusion. Our approach computes the dynamics of higher-order moments and fluctuation statistics without explicitly evolving the quantum state, thereby providing an efficient and scalable approach for investigating many-body open quantum systems. We demonstrate the versatility of the formalism by applying it to both the integrable open XXZ chain and the nonintegrable open next-nearest-neighbor XXZ spin chain, where it uncovers distinct initial state dependent long-time transport regimes. Our work establishes quantum generating functions as an efficient and scalable framework for investigating long-time dynamics in open quantum many-body systems.
summary: This paper introduces the Quantum Generating Function (QGF) formalism to overcome the computational bottleneck of simulating long-time dynamics in open quantum many-body systems. By calculating moments without evolving the full quantum state, the authors successfully characterize transport phenomena in spin chains. This establishes QGF as a robust and scalable method for studying non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is efficiently simulating the long-time dynamics of many-body open quantum systems, where conventional methods struggle due to Hilbert space growth.
main_result: The Quantum Generating Function (QGF) formalism provides an efficient and scalable framework to compute higher-order moments and fluctuation statistics for open systems, successfully characterizing distinct initial state-dependent transport regimes in XXZ and nnn-XXZ chains.
method: The authors developed and applied the QGF formalism, which computes dynamics via Fourier transformation of the probability distribution, allowing moment extraction without explicitly evolving the full quantum state.
model_or_system: The study focuses on open quantum many-body systems, specifically using the XXZ and next-nearest-neighbor XXZ spin chains. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating both unitary evolution and environmental dissipation (e.g., local injection or dephasing).
key_observables: Higher-order moments ($\mu_n(t)$) of transferred magnetization, fluctuation statistics ($\kappa_2(t)$), and the identification of transport regimes (ballistic, diffusive, superdiffusive).
important_parameters: The counting field $\lambda$, the injection rate $\Gamma_G$, and the initial state (Néel, Ising-type, fully polarized).
main_assumptions: The approach relies on the GKSL quantum master equation framework for open dynamics, and moment extraction via QGF assumes convergence of the perturbative expansion in $\lambda$.
figures_summary: Figures compare the first and second moments of transferred magnetization ($\mu_1(t), \mu_2(t)$) for XXZ and nnn-XXZ chains, contrasting QGF results against state-evolution methods (MPS) and showing different scaling behaviors for different initial states.
paper_structure: The paper develops the QGF formalism, proves its equivalence to Full Counting Statistics (FCS) derived from quantum jump trajectories, and then applies it to model open dynamics in spin chains, comparing results across different initial conditions and Hamiltonian types.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, scalable theoretical tool (QGF) to analyze non-equilibrium dynamics in complex quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding energy/particle transport in quantum materials.
